_ P_ o_ w_ e_ r _ C_ a_ l_ c_ u_ l_ a_ t_ i_ o_ n _ i_ n _ t_ h_ e _ A_ n_ a_ l_ y_ s_ i_ s _ o_ f _ S_ u_ r_ v_ i_ v_ a_ l _ D_ a_ t_ a _ f_ o_ r _ C_ l_ i_ n_ i_ c_ a_ l _ T_ r_ i_ a_ l_ s

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Power calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves Between
     Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for clinical
     trials.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     powerCT.default(nE, 
                     nC, 
                     pE, 
                     pC, 
                     RR, 
                     alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

      nE: integer. number of participants in the experimental group.

      nC: integer. number of participants in the control group.

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)
          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     The power of the test.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     The power formula assumes that the central-limit theorem is valid
     and hence is appropriate for large samples.

_ R_ e_ f_ e_ r_ e_ n_ c_ e_ s:

     Freedman, L.S. (1982).  Tables of the number of patients required
     in clinical trials using the log-rank test.  _Statistics in
     Medicine_. 1: 121-129

     Rosner B. (2006).  _Fundamentals of Biostatistics_. (6-th
     edition). Thomson Brooks/Cole.

plan.estimand: Risk difference in cluster-level rates (per child-week exposure)
plan.hypothesis: Treatment rate ≠ control rate; two-sided test of equality
assumptions: Cluster rates follow a mixed-model distribution with exponential (Poisson) within-cluster variability and log-normal between-cluster heterogeneity
Between-cluster coefficient of variation κ = 0.15 characterizes multiplicative random effects on the cluster-level rate parameter
Additive one-cluster correction is applied to stabilize variance estimation in small-sample designs
Exposure is balanced within clusters (2500 child-weeks per cluster)
Equal allocation ratio (1:1) across treatment and control arms
Two-sided Wald-type or score-based test with nominal α = 0.05
Asymptotic normal approximation is valid for the cluster-aggregated rate estimates
scientific_notes: The cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation method addresses between-cluster heterogeneity in incidence rates, critical when cluster-level rate variability is substantial relative to the target effect size
Additive one-cluster correction (adding 1 to the count of clusters in variance calculations) reduces bias in variance estimation when the number of clusters is small (e.g., k < 10 per arm)
Treatment and control rates are both specified per unit exposure (child-week), enabling direct comparison on a uniform rate scale
Risk difference Δ = 0.005 − 0.010 = −0.005 per child-week; absolute effect magnitude is 50% relative reduction
Output will be the smallest integer k (clusters per arm) that achieves at least 90% power under the specified conditions

answer.summary: Using the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation with additive one-cluster correction, the minimum number of clusters per arm to achieve 90% power for detecting a two-sided difference in rates (treatment 0.005 vs. control 0.010 per child-week, with 2500 child-weeks per cluster, between-cluster CV = 0.15, alpha = 0.05, equal allocation) is **6446 clusters per arm**. This design yields an achieved power of 0.900031, exceeding the 0.90 target. The preceding design (6445 clusters) achieves power of 0.899987, falling short of the target.
answer.method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation with additive one-cluster correction. The variance of cluster-level rates is modeled as var(λ | κ) = λ(1 + κ²), accounting for Poisson within-cluster variability and multiplicative log-normal between-cluster random effects. The sample size formula (uncorrected continuous) is k = [(z_{α/2} + z_β)² × (p_t + p_c)(1 + κ²)] / δ², where δ = p_t − p_c is the risk difference, κ = 0.15 is the between-cluster CV, and z_{α/2} = 1.9600, z_β = 1.2816 for two-sided α = 0.05 and target power 0.90. The additive one-cluster correction subtracts 1 from this continuous result before rounding to integer. Power is calculated using the non-centrality parameter approach for a two-sided test: Power = Φ(z_{α/2}, ncp) + Φ(−z_{α/2}, ncp), where ncp = |δ| / SE(δ) and SE(δ) = √[combined_var / (k+1)].
assumptions: Cluster rates follow a mixed-model distribution with Poisson within-cluster variability and log-normal between-cluster random effects
Between-cluster coefficient of variation κ = 0.15 characterizes multiplicative random effects on the cluster-level rate parameter and is constant across treatment and control arms
Additive one-cluster correction (k_eff = k + 1) is applied to stabilize variance estimation in cluster designs
Exposure is balanced within clusters (exactly 2500 child-weeks per cluster) with no loss to follow-up
Equal allocation ratio (1:1) across treatment and control arms
Two-sided Wald-type test with nominal α = 0.05 for hypothesis H0: λ_treatment = λ_control
Asymptotic normal approximation is valid for cluster-aggregated rate estimates (justified by large expected event counts: ~12.5 in treatment, ~25 in control per cluster)
No interaction between treatment and cluster-level random effects; proportional hazards assumption on the rate scale
limitations: The cluster-rate CV approximation assumes a specific variance structure (1 + κ²) that may not capture all sources of heterogeneity in cluster-level rates
The method does not account for potential cluster-by-treatment interactions in the between-cluster variability
The additive one-cluster correction is a heuristic small-sample adjustment with limited theoretical justification in the rate context; for very large designs (k >> 100) its impact diminishes
The calculation assumes exact adherence to the exposure schedule (2500 child-weeks per cluster); deviations would require adjustment
No provision for adjusting sample size for anticipated attrition, protocol deviations, or missing data
Estimates assume that the specified treatment and control rates are known without estimation error prior to the trial

The approach is most appropriate for designs with moderate cluster sizes and moderate between-cluster variation; extreme values of κ or very small expected event counts may violate asymptotic assumptions

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation
# with additive one-cluster correction for sample size calculation
# 
# Reference: Hayes & Moulton (2009) and related cluster-randomized trial methods
# Input parameters
p_t <- 0.005        # Treatment rate (events per child-week)
p_c <- 0.010        # Control rate (events per child-week)
E <- 2500           # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.15       # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05       # Two-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.90 # Target power
ratio <- 1          # Allocation ratio (1:1)

# For two-sided test with equal allocation
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)      # One-sided critical value for power

# Risk difference
delta <- p_t - p_c  # = -0.005 per child-week

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu_t <- p_t * E     # Treatment: 0.005 * 2500 = 12.5 events
mu_c <- p_c * E     # Control: 0.010 * 2500 = 25 events

# Variance under Poisson within-cluster + between-cluster CV
# For a rate parameter lambda with CV κ, the variance is (1 + κ^2) * lambda
# This accounts for: Poisson variance = lambda + extra-Poisson variance = lambda * κ^2

# Variance per cluster for treatment (per child-week scale)
var_t_per_unit <- p_t * (1 + kappa^2)  # Variance of rate per child-week

# Variance per cluster for control
var_c_per_unit <- p_c * (1 + kappa^2)

# Variance of cluster-level total counts
var_t_count <- (var_t_per_unit) * E    # Variance of total events in treatment cluster
var_c_count <- (var_c_per_unit) * E    # Variance of total events in control cluster

# Variance of cluster-level rates (counting expected events E per cluster)
# var(delta_hat) = var_t/n_t + var_c/n_c for risk difference
# where var_t = var(total events in treatment cluster) / E^2

# For cluster-aggregated rate difference estimator:
# var(p_t_hat) = (p_t * (1 + kappa^2)) / n_t  per cluster
# var(p_c_hat) = (p_c * (1 + kappa^2)) / n_c  per cluster

# Standard error squared of risk difference with k clusters per arm:
# SE^2(delta_hat) = [p_t * (1 + κ^2) + p_c * (1 + κ^2)] / k (for equal allocation)

# Additive one-cluster correction: k_eff = k + 1
# This corrects the variance estimate by replacing k with (k + 1) in the denominator

# Sample size formula (before rounding, without correction):
# n = 2 * (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * (p_t * (1 + κ^2) + p_c * (1 + κ^2)) / (delta)^2
# Note: 2 factor accounts for having 2 arms (k per arm)

# Combined variance (per arm, using rate scale)
combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)

# Uncorrected sample size formula (continuous)
k_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)

cat("=== Cluster-Rate CV Approximation with One-Cluster Correction ===\n\n")
cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate (p_t): %.4f events/child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate (p_c):   %.4f events/child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference:      %.4f events/child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster: %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV:   %.4f\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Two-sided alpha:      %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power:         %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:     %d:1\n", ratio))
cat("\nStatistical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2) [two-sided]:  %.4f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_β [power]:          %.4f\n", z_beta))
cat("\nVariance Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  p_t * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_t * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  p_c * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  Combined variance:    %.6f\n", combined_var))
cat("\nSample Size Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  (z_α/2 + z_β)²:       %.4f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator (z sum)² * var: %.6f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var))
cat(sprintf("  (delta)²:             %.8f\n", delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (uncorrected): %.4f\n", k_continuous))

# With additive one-cluster correction: solve for k such that (k + 1) satisfies power
# We need: (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / (k_corrected) = delta^2
# where k_corrected = k + 1
# So: k + 1 = (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / delta^2
# Thus: k = [(z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / delta^2] - 1

k_corrected_continuous <- k_continuous - 1

cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (one-cluster corrected): %.4f\n", k_corrected_continuous))

# Find minimum integer k that meets power requirement
# Check power at integer values
power_check <- function(k) {
  k_eff <- k + 1  # Additive one-cluster correction
  se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
  z_stat <- abs(delta) / se_delta
  power <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(z_alpha_2 - z_stat))  # Two-sided power
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum k
k_min <- 1
k_test <- seq(1, 30)
powers <- sapply(k_test, power_check)

# Find smallest k with power >= target
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
k_optimal <- k_test[idx]
power_at_optimal <- powers[idx]

# Also check preceding value for context
k_preceding <- k_optimal - 1
power_at_preceding <- if (k_preceding >= 1) power_check(k_preceding) else NA

cat("\n=== Integer Sample Size Search ===\n")
cat("Clusters/Arm | Achieved Power\n")
for (i in which(k_test %in% c(k_preceding, k_optimal, k_optimal+1))) {
  if (!is.na(k_test[i])) {
    cat(sprintf("     %2d      |    %.4f\n", k_test[i], powers[i]))
  }
}

cat(sprintf("\n*** RESULT: %d clusters per arm ***\n", k_optimal))
cat(sprintf("    Achieved power: %.4f\n", power_at_optimal))
if (k_preceding >= 1) {
  cat(sprintf("    Power at k=%d (preceding): %.4f\n", k_preceding, power_at_preceding))
}

# Output for structured reporting
results_df <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = k_optimal,
  unit = "clusters_per_arm"
)

cat("\n=== Structured Output ===\n")
print(results_df)

mu_c <- p_c * E     # Control: 0.010 * 2500 = 25 events

var_c_per_unit <- p_c * (1 + kappa^2)

combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)

cat("\nVariance Calculation:\n")

cat(sprintf("  p_c * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))

cat("\nSample Size Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  (z_α/2 + z_β)²:       %.4f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator (z sum)² * var: %.6f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var))
cat(sprintf("  (delta)²:             %.8f\n", delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (uncorrected): %.4f\n", k_continuous))

# with additive one-cluster correction for sample size calculation
# 
# CORRECTED power formula for two-sided test
# Input parameters
p_t <- 0.005        # Treatment rate (events per child-week)
p_c <- 0.010        # Control rate (events per child-week)
E <- 2500           # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.15       # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05       # Two-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.90 # Target power
ratio <- 1          # Allocation ratio (1:1)

# For two-sided test with equal allocation
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)      # One-sided critical value for power

# Risk difference
delta <- p_t - p_c  # = -0.005 per child-week

# Combined variance (per arm, using rate scale)
combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)

# Uncorrected sample size formula (continuous)
k_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)

cat("=== Cluster-Rate CV Approximation with One-Cluster Correction ===\n\n")
cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate (p_t): %.4f events/child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate (p_c):   %.4f events/child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference:      %.4f events/child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster: %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV:   %.4f\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Two-sided alpha:      %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power:         %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:     %d:1\n", ratio))
cat("\nStatistical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2) [two-sided]:  %.4f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_β [power]:          %.4f\n", z_beta))
cat("\nVariance Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  p_t * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_t * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  p_c * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  Combined variance:    %.6f\n", combined_var))
cat("\nSample Size Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  (z_α/2 + z_β)²:       %.4f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator (z sum)² * var: %.6f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var))
cat(sprintf("  |delta|²:             %.8f\n", delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (uncorrected): %.4f\n", k_continuous))

# With additive one-cluster correction
k_corrected_continuous <- k_continuous - 1

cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (one-cluster corrected): %.4f\n", k_corrected_continuous))

# Corrected power function for two-sided test
# H0: delta = 0 vs H1: delta != 0
# Test statistic: Z = delta_hat / SE(delta_hat)
# Reject H0 if |Z| > z_alpha/2
# Power = P(|Z| > z_alpha/2 | H1 is true)
#       = P(Z > z_alpha/2) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2)
# Under H1: Z ~ N(delta / SE, 1)
# Power = P(Z - delta/SE > z_alpha/2 - delta/SE) + P(Z - delta/SE < -z_alpha/2 - delta/SE)
#       = 1 - Phi(z_alpha/2 - delta/SE) + Phi(-z_alpha/2 - delta/SE)

power_check <- function(k) {
  k_eff <- k + 1  # Additive one-cluster correction
  se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
  
  # Standardized effect size
  ncp <- abs(delta) / se_delta  # Non-centrality parameter
  
  # Two-sided power: P(|Z| > z_alpha/2 | effect exists)
  # = 1 - Phi(z_alpha/2 - ncp) + Phi(-z_alpha/2 - ncp)
  # = 1 - Phi(z_alpha/2 - ncp) - Phi(z_alpha/2 - ncp)  [if effect is positive]
  # Simpler: Power = 1 - Phi(z_alpha/2 - ncp) + Phi(-z_alpha/2 - ncp)
  
  # For a two-sided test with effect in one direction:
  power <- 1 - pnorm(z_alpha_2 - ncp) + pnorm(-z_alpha_2 - ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Alternative simpler formulation (correct):
# Under H1: delta_hat ~ N(delta, SE^2)
# Z = delta_hat / SE ~ N(delta/SE, 1) = N(ncp, 1)
# Reject if |Z| > z_alpha/2
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha/2) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2)
#       = 1 - Phi(z_alpha/2 - ncp) + Phi(-z_alpha/2 - ncp)
# But if we're testing H0: lambda_t = lambda_c vs H1: lambda_t != lambda_c
# and delta < 0 (treatment lower), then the power is:
# Power = P(Z < -z_alpha/2 - ncp) under the alternative

# Let me rewrite more carefully:
power_check_v2 <- function(k) {
  k_eff <- k + 1
  se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
  ncp <- abs(delta) / se_delta
  
  # Two-sided test power
  # Reject H0 if |test_stat| > z_alpha/2
  # Under H1: test_stat ~ N(delta/SE, 1)
  # Power = P(test_stat > z_alpha/2 or test_stat < -z_alpha/2)
  #       = pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
  #         pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
  
  power <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum k starting from a reasonable range
k_base <- floor(k_corrected_continuous)
k_test <- seq(max(1, k_base - 5), k_base + 10, by = 1)

powers <- sapply(k_test, power_check_v2)

# Find smallest k with power >= target
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)
k_optimal <- k_test[idx[1]]
power_at_optimal <- power_check_v2(k_optimal)

# Check preceding value for context
k_preceding <- k_optimal - 1
if (k_preceding >= 1) {
  power_at_preceding <- power_check_v2(k_preceding)
} else {
  power_at_preceding <- NA
}

cat("\n=== Integer Sample Size Search ===\n")
cat("Clusters/Arm | Achieved Power\n")
cat(paste(rep("-", 35), collapse = ""), "\n")

# Show a few key values
show_k <- c(k_preceding, k_optimal, k_optimal+1)
show_k <- show_k[show_k >= 1]
for (k_val in show_k) {
  pow_val <- power_check_v2(k_val)
  marker <- if (k_val == k_optimal) " <-- SELECTED" else ""
  cat(sprintf("     %4d      |    %.6f %s\n", k_val, pow_val, marker))
}

cat(sprintf("\n*** RESULT: %d clusters per arm ***\n", k_optimal))
cat(sprintf("    Achieved power: %.6f\n", power_at_optimal))
if (!is.na(power_at_preceding)) {
  cat(sprintf("    Power at k=%d (preceding): %.6f\n", k_preceding, power_at_preceding))
}

cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2):                   %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  Achieved power:            %.6f\n", power_verified))

# Output for structured reporting
cat("\n=== JSON Output for Structured Reporting ===\n")
output_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_optimal, unit = "clusters_per_arm")

  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

# Detailed verification and summary of the cluster-rate CV method
# This documents the statistical approach and validates the result

cat("=== METHODOLOGICAL DETAILS ===\n\n")

cat("Study Design: Cluster-Randomized Trial\n")
cat("Primary Estimand: Risk Difference in Cluster-Level Rates (per child-week)\n")
cat("Unit of Randomization: Cluster (multiple child-weeks nested within clusters)\n\n")

cat("Hypothesis Test:\n")
cat("  H0: λ_treatment = λ_control (rates equal across arms)\n")
cat("  H1: λ_treatment ≠ λ_control (two-sided alternative)\n")
cat("  Significance level: α = 0.05 (two-sided)\n\n")

cat("Analytical Method: Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation Approximation\n")
cat("  Reference: Hayes & Moulton (2009) and variations thereof\n")
cat("  Accounts for: Between-cluster heterogeneity in rate parameters\n")
cat("  Correction: Additive one-cluster correction to variance estimate\n\n")

# Parameters
p_t <- 0.005
p_c <- 0.010
E <- 2500
kappa <- 0.15
delta <- p_t - p_c

cat("Effect Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate λ_t:        %g per child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate λ_c:          %g per child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference (δ):       %g per child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Relative difference:       %.1f%% (treatment vs control)\n", 100 * delta / p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Expected events/cluster (treatment):  %.1f\n", p_t * E))
cat(sprintf("  Expected events/cluster (control):    %.1f\n", p_c * E))
cat("\nNuisance/Design Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster (E):  %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV (κ):    %.3f (multiplicative random effect)\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:          1:1 (equal allocation)\n\n")

z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - 0.05 / 2)
z_beta <- qnorm(0.90)

cat("Critical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2) = z_%.4f:         %.6f [two-sided rejection boundary]\n", 0.975, z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_β = z_%.4f:              %.6f [power-based quantile]\n", 0.90, z_beta))
cat(sprintf("  (z_(α/2) + z_β)²:          %.6f\n\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))

cat("Variance Calculation (Rate Scale):\n")
cat("  Under mixed model (Poisson within + log-normal between clusters):\n")
cat("    var(λ | κ) = λ × (1 + κ²)\n\n")

combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)
cat(sprintf("  For treatment rate:   var = %g × (1 + %.4f²) = %.6f\n", 
            p_t, kappa, p_t * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  For control rate:     var = %g × (1 + %.4f²) = %.6f\n", 
            p_c, kappa, p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  Combined (p_t + p_c)(1 + κ²): %.6f\n\n", combined_var))

k_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)
k_corrected <- k_continuous - 1

cat("Sample Size Calculation (Continuous):\n")
cat("  Formula: k = [(z_(α/2) + z_β)² × Var(Δ)] / (Δ)²\n")
cat(sprintf("         k = [%.4f × %.6f] / %.8f\n",
            (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2, combined_var, delta^2))
cat(sprintf("         k = %.4f clusters/arm (uncorrected)\n\n", k_continuous))

cat("One-Cluster Additive Correction:\n")
cat("  Rationale: Small-sample bias reduction in variance estimate\n")
cat("    k_corrected = k - 1 (subtracts 1 cluster from uncorrected count)\n")
cat(sprintf("    k_corrected = %.4f - 1 = %.4f clusters/arm\n\n", k_continuous, k_corrected))

cat("Integer Rounding:\n")
cat("  Minimum integer meeting target power:\n")
cat("    k = 6446 clusters per arm\n")
cat("    (both arms combined: N = 12,892 clusters)\n")
cat("    Total child-week exposure: 12,892 × 2,500 = 32,230,000 child-weeks\n\n")

# Validation at selected design

k_eff <- k_opt + 1
se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
ncp <- abs(delta) / se_delta
power_achieved <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
                  pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)

cat("Power Verification at k = 6446:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effective n (k+1):              %d\n", k_eff))
cat(sprintf("  SE(Δ):                          %.8f per child-week\n", se_delta))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter:       %.6f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("  P(reject H0 | H1 true):        %.6f [two-sided]\n", power_achieved))
cat(sprintf("  Target power achieved:          ✓ (%.4f ≥ 0.90)\n\n", power_achieved))

# Preceding design
k_prec <- 6445
k_eff_prec <- k_prec + 1

# Detailed verification and summary of the cluster-rate CV method

cat("=== METHODOLOGICAL DETAILS ===\n\n")

cat("Study Design: Cluster-Randomized Trial\n")
cat("Primary Estimand: Risk Difference in Cluster-Level Rates (per child-week)\n")
cat("Unit of Randomization: Cluster (multiple child-weeks nested within clusters)\n\n")

cat("Hypothesis Test:\n")
cat("  H0: lambda_treatment = lambda_control (rates equal across arms)\n")
cat("  H1: lambda_treatment != lambda_control (two-sided alternative)\n")
cat("  Significance level: alpha = 0.05 (two-sided)\n\n")

cat("Analytical Method: Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation Approximation\n")
cat("  Reference: Hayes and Moulton (2009) and variations thereof\n")
cat("  Accounts for: Between-cluster heterogeneity in rate parameters\n")
cat("  Correction: Additive one-cluster correction to variance estimate\n\n")

# Parameters
p_t <- 0.005
p_c <- 0.010
E <- 2500
kappa <- 0.15
delta <- p_t - p_c

cat("Effect Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate (lambda_t):     %.4f per child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate (lambda_c):       %.4f per child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference (delta):       %.4f per child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Relative difference:           %.1f%% (treatment vs control)\n", 100 * delta / p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Expected events/cluster (tx):  %.1f\n", p_t * E))
cat(sprintf("  Expected events/cluster (cx):  %.1f\n", p_c * E))
cat("\nNuisance/Design Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster (E):      %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV (kappa):    %.3f (multiplicative random effect)\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:              1:1 (equal allocation)\n\n"))

z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - 0.05 / 2)
z_beta <- qnorm(0.90)

cat("Critical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(alpha/2) = z_0.975:        %.6f [two-sided rejection boundary]\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_beta = z_0.90:              %.6f [power-based quantile]\n", z_beta))
cat(sprintf("  (z_(alpha/2) + z_beta)^2:     %.6f\n\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))

cat("Variance Calculation (Rate Scale):\n")
cat("  Under mixed model (Poisson within + log-normal between clusters):\n")
cat("    var(lambda | kappa) = lambda * (1 + kappa^2)\n\n")

combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)
cat(sprintf("  For treatment rate:   var = %.4f * (1 + %.4f^2) = %.6f\n", 
            p_t, kappa, p_t * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  For control rate:     var = %.4f * (1 + %.4f^2) = %.6f\n", 
            p_c, kappa, p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  Combined (p_t + p_c)(1 + kappa^2): %.6f\n\n", combined_var))

k_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)
k_corrected <- k_continuous - 1

cat("Sample Size Calculation (Continuous):\n")
cat("  Formula: k = [(z_(alpha/2) + z_beta)^2 * Var(delta)] / (delta)^2\n")
cat(sprintf("         k = [%.4f * %.6f] / %.8f\n",
            (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2, combined_var, delta^2))
cat(sprintf("         k = %.4f clusters/arm (uncorrected)\n\n", k_continuous))

cat("One-Cluster Additive Correction:\n")
cat("  Rationale: Small-sample bias reduction in variance estimate\n")
cat("    k_corrected = k - 1 (subtracts 1 cluster from uncorrected count)\n")
cat(sprintf("    k_corrected = %.4f - 1 = %.4f clusters/arm\n\n", k_continuous, k_corrected))

cat("Integer Rounding:\n")
cat("  Minimum integer meeting target power:\n")
cat("    k = 6446 clusters per arm\n")
cat("    (both arms combined: N = 12,892 clusters)\n")
cat("    Total child-week exposure: 12,892 x 2,500 = 32,230,000 child-weeks\n\n")

# Validation at selected design
k_opt <- 6446
k_eff <- k_opt + 1
se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
ncp <- abs(delta) / se_delta
power_achieved <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
                  pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)

cat("Power Verification at k = 6446:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effective n (k+1):              %d\n", k_eff))
cat(sprintf("  SE(delta):                      %.8f per child-week\n", se_delta))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter:       %.6f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("  P(reject H0 | H1 true):        %.6f [two-sided]\n", power_achieved))
cat(sprintf("  Target power achieved:          YES (%.4f >= 0.90)\n\n", power_achieved))

# Preceding design
k_prec <- 6445
k_eff_prec <- k_prec + 1
se_delta_prec <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff_prec)
ncp_prec <- abs(delta) / se_delta_prec
power_prec <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_prec, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
              pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_prec, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)

cat("Power at Preceding Design (k = 6445):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effective n (k+1):              %d\n", k_eff_prec))
cat(sprintf("  SE(delta):                      %.8f per child-week\n", se_delta_prec))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter:       %.6f\n", ncp_prec))
cat(sprintf("  P(reject H0 | H1 true):        %.6f [two-sided]\n", power_prec))
cat(sprintf("  Target power met:               NO (%.6f < 0.90)\n\n", power_prec))

cat("Summary: Power Across Candidate Designs\n")
cat("Design (k) | Effective n | SE(delta)  | Power\n")
cat(paste(rep("-", 50), collapse = ""), "\n")
cat(sprintf("  6445   |     6446    | %.8f | %.6f\n", se_delta_prec, power_prec))
cat(sprintf("  6446   |     6447    | %.8f | %.6f [SELECTED]\n", se_delta, power_achieved))
cat(sprintf("  6447   |     6448    | %.8f | %.6f\n", 
            sqrt(combined_var / 6448),
            pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = abs(delta)/sqrt(combined_var / 6448), sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
            pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = abs(delta)/sqrt(combined_var / 6448), sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)))

cat("\n=== KEY ASSUMPTIONS ===\n")
cat("1. Cluster rates follow a mixed-effect Poisson model:\n")
cat("   - Poisson within-cluster variability\n")
cat("   - Log-normal between-cluster random effects\n\n")
cat("2. Between-cluster CV kappa = 0.15 is constant across arms\n\n")

cat("4. Asymptotic normality valid (justified by large exposure: 2500 child-weeks/cluster)\n\n")
cat("5. Balanced exposure across clusters; no attrition\n\n")

cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm (integer, minimum for 90% power): 6446\n")
cat("Total clusters (both arms): 12,892\n")
cat("Total child-week exposure: 32,230,000\n")

# Independent verification of the cluster-rate CV approximation result
# Using the formula and corrected two-sided power calculation

# Study parameters (from request)
p_t <- 0.005         # treatment rate (events per child-week)
p_c <- 0.010         # control rate (events per child-week)
E <- 2500            # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.15        # between-cluster CV
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90 # target power
delta <- p_t - p_c   # risk difference = -0.005

# Critical values
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # 1.9600
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)     # 1.2816

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  p_t = %g, p_c = %g, delta = %g\n", p_t, p_c, delta))
cat(sprintf("  E = %d, kappa = %.3f\n", E, kappa))
cat(sprintf("  alpha = %.4f (two-sided), target power = %.2f\n", alpha, target_power))
cat(sprintf("  z_(alpha/2) = %.6f, z_beta = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, z_beta))

# Variance structure
# For rate lambda with between-cluster CV kappa:
# var(lambda) = lambda * (1 + kappa^2)

combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)
cat(sprintf("\nVariance of rate difference:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Combined var = (%.4f + %.4f) * (1 + %.4f^2) = %.6f\n", 
            p_t, p_c, kappa, combined_var))

# Sample size formula (uncorrected)
# k = [(z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * var] / (delta^2)
k_uncorrected <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)

cat(sprintf("\nUncorrected sample size:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  k = [(%.6f + %.6f)^2 * %.6f] / (%.8f)^2\n",
            z_alpha_2, z_beta, combined_var, delta))
cat(sprintf("  k = [%.6f * %.6f] / %.8f\n",
            (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2, combined_var, delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  k = %.4f clusters/arm (uncorrected)\n", k_uncorrected))

# Apply one-cluster correction (subtract 1)
k_corrected_continuous <- k_uncorrected - 1
cat(sprintf("\nWith additive one-cluster correction:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  k_corrected = %.4f - 1 = %.4f\n", k_uncorrected, k_corrected_continuous))

# Now find minimum integer k meeting power requirement
# Power function for two-sided test:
# Under H1 (delta ≠ 0): test statistic ~ N(delta/SE, 1)
# Reject H0 if |test_stat| > z_alpha/2
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha/2) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2) where Z ~ N(delta/SE, 1)

power_calc <- function(k) {
  k_eff <- k + 1  # effective clusters with correction
  se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
  ncp <- abs(delta) / se_delta  # non-centrality
  
  # Two-sided power: probability of rejecting H0 under alternative
  # = P(Z > z_alpha/2 | Z ~ N(ncp, 1)) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2 | Z ~ N(ncp, 1))
  pow <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
         pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
  
  return(pow)
}

# Search around the corrected continuous value
k_start <- floor(k_corrected_continuous) - 2
k_end <- floor(k_corrected_continuous) + 5
k_search <- seq(k_start, k_end, by = 1)

powers <- sapply(k_search, power_calc)

cat(sprintf("\n=== POWER SEARCH ===\n"))
cat("k (clusters/arm) | Power (two-sided)\n")
cat(paste(rep("-", 35), collapse = ""), "\n")
for (i in seq_along(k_search)) {
  marker <- if (powers[i] >= target_power & (i == 1 || powers[i-1] < target_power)) " <-- MINIMUM" else ""
  cat(sprintf("    %5d        | %.6f%s\n", k_search[i], powers[i], marker))
}

# Find minimum k
idx_min <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
k_minimum <- k_search[idx_min]
power_at_minimum <- powers[idx_min]
power_preceding <- if (idx_min > 1) powers[idx_min - 1] else NA

cat(sprintf("\n=== RESULT ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Minimum integer k (clusters per arm): %d\n", k_minimum))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f (target: %.2f)\n", power_at_minimum, target_power))
if (!is.na(power_preceding)) {
  cat(sprintf("Power at k=%d (preceding): %.6f\n", k_minimum - 1, power_preceding))
}

# Detailed verification at k=6446
cat(sprintf("\n=== VERIFICATION AT k = %d ===\n", k_minimum))
k_eff_min <- k_minimum + 1
se_min <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff_min)
ncp_min <- abs(delta) / se_min

cat(sprintf("Effective clusters (k+1): %d\n", k_eff_min))
cat(sprintf("SE(delta): %.8f\n", se_min))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality: %.6f\n", ncp_min))
cat(sprintf("z_alpha/2: %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("P(Z > z_alpha/2 | ncp): %.6f\n", 
            pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_min, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)))
cat(sprintf("P(Z < -z_alpha/2 | ncp): %.6f\n",
            pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_min, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Total power (two-sided): %.6f\n", power_at_minimum))

# Compare with candidate answer
cat(sprintf("\n=== COMPARISON WITH CANDIDATE ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Candidate reported: k = 6446, power = 0.900031\n"))
cat(sprintf("Independent verification: k = %d, power = %.6f\n", k_minimum, power_at_minimum))
cat(sprintf("Match: %s\n", if (k_minimum == 6446 && abs(power_at_minimum - 0.900031) < 0.00001) "YES" else "NO"))

# Emit structured output
output_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_minimum, unit = "clusters_per_arm")
  )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)
cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=%s\n", output_json))

# and that the one-cluster correction formula is properly applied

cat("=== DETAILED POWER FORMULA VERIFICATION ===\n\n")

p_t <- 0.005
p_c <- 0.010
delta <- p_t - p_c
kappa <- 0.15
alpha <- 0.05
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)

k <- 6446
k_eff <- k + 1

# Standard error of delta_hat
se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)

cat("Setup:\n")
cat(sprintf("  k = %d clusters per arm\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  k_eff = k + 1 = %d (with one-cluster correction)\n", k_eff))
cat(sprintf("  SE(delta) = sqrt(%.6f / %d) = %.8f\n", combined_var, k_eff, se_delta))

cat("\nTwo-Sided Test Power Calculation:\n")
cat("  H0: delta = 0 vs H1: delta != 0\n")
cat("  Reject H0 if |delta_hat / SE| > z_alpha/2\n\n")

# Test statistic under H1: Z = delta_hat / SE
# Under H1, delta_hat is an estimate of delta = -0.005
# So Z = delta / SE + (delta_hat - delta) / SE
# E[Z | H1] = delta / SE = -0.005 / SE
# The test statistic Z is approximately N(delta/SE, 1)

ncp_raw <- delta / se_delta  # Should be negative
ncp_abs <- abs(delta) / se_delta  # Use absolute value for NCP

cat(sprintf("  Test statistic Z under H1: Z ~ N(delta/SE, 1) = N(%f, 1)\n", ncp_raw))
cat(sprintf("  |delta|/SE = %.6f (absolute non-centrality)\n", ncp_abs))

cat("\nPower Calculation (Method 1: Integrate over both tails):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Power = P(Z > z_alpha/2) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2) | H1 true\n"))
cat(sprintf("        = P(Z > %.6f) + P(Z < %.6f) where Z ~ N(%.6f, 1)\n",
            z_alpha_2, -z_alpha_2, ncp_raw))

# P(Z > z_alpha/2) where Z ~ N(delta/SE, 1)
# = P(Z - delta/SE > z_alpha/2 - delta/SE)
# = P(std_normal > z_alpha/2 - delta/SE)
# = 1 - Phi(z_alpha/2 - delta/SE)

p_upper <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_raw, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
p_lower <- pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_raw, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
power_method1 <- p_upper + p_lower

cat(sprintf("  P(Z > %.6f | ncp=%.6f) = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, ncp_raw, p_upper))
cat(sprintf("  P(Z < %.6f | ncp=%.6f) = %.6f\n", -z_alpha_2, ncp_raw, p_lower))
cat(sprintf("  Total power: %.6f\n\n", power_method1))

cat("Power Calculation (Method 2: Using absolute NCP):\n")
# This is equivalent when we account for direction
# P(|Z| > z_alpha/2 | Z ~ N(ncp, 1)) 
# When ncp > 0:
p_upper_abs <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_abs, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
p_lower_abs <- pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_abs, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
power_method2 <- p_upper_abs + p_lower_abs

cat(sprintf("  P(Z > %.6f | ncp=%.6f) = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, ncp_abs, p_upper_abs))
cat(sprintf("  P(Z < %.6f | ncp=%.6f) = %.6f\n", -z_alpha_2, ncp_abs, p_lower_abs))
cat(sprintf("  Total power: %.6f\n\n", power_method2))

cat("Consistency check:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Method 1 (signed NCP): %.6f\n", power_method1))
cat(sprintf("  Method 2 (absolute NCP): %.6f\n", power_method2))
cat(sprintf("  Agree: %s\n\n", if (abs(power_method1 - power_method2) < 1e-10) "YES" else "NO"))

# Verify this matches candidate output
cat("Comparison with candidate e4 output:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Candidate reported power at k=6446: 0.900031\n"))
cat(sprintf("  This calculation yields: %.6f\n", power_method1))
cat(sprintf("  Match: %s\n\n", if (abs(power_method1 - 0.900031) < 0.00001) "YES" else "NO"))

# Now check the one-cluster correction formula interpretation
cat("=== ONE-CLUSTER CORRECTION INTERPRETATION ===\n\n")
cat("The additive one-cluster correction is applied as follows:\n")
cat("  Uncorrected formula: k = [(z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * Var] / (delta)^2\n")
cat("  This gives k as the number of clusters per arm\n\n")
cat("  With one-cluster correction:\n")
cat("    k_corrected = k - 1\n")
cat("    This effectively increases the effective sample size in power\n")
cat("    calculations, as we use k_eff = k + 1 in the variance\n\n")
cat("  Interpretation:\n")
cat("    When k = k_uncorrected, power just barely fails to meet target\n")
cat("    Adding 1 cluster (k = k_uncorrected) with the correction gives\n")

se_no_corr <- sqrt(combined_var / k_no_corr)  # Without +1
ncp_no_corr <- abs(delta) / se_no_corr

cat(sprintf("Verification: Power at k=6446 WITHOUT correction (no +1):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  SE = sqrt(%.6f / %d) = %.8f\n", combined_var, k_no_corr, se_no_corr))

plan.estimand: Risk difference in cluster-level rates (per child-week exposure)
plan.hypothesis: Treatment rate ≠ control rate; two-sided test of equality
assumptions: Cluster rates follow a mixed-model distribution with exponential (Poisson) within-cluster variability and log-normal between-cluster heterogeneity
Between-cluster coefficient of variation κ = 0.15 characterizes multiplicative random effects on the cluster-level rate parameter
Additive one-cluster correction is applied to stabilize variance estimation in small-sample designs
Exposure is balanced within clusters (2500 child-weeks per cluster)
Equal allocation ratio (1:1) across treatment and control arms
Two-sided Wald-type or score-based test with nominal α = 0.05
Asymptotic normal approximation is valid for the cluster-aggregated rate estimates
scientific_notes: The cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation method addresses between-cluster heterogeneity in incidence rates, critical when cluster-level rate variability is substantial relative to the target effect size
Additive one-cluster correction (adding 1 to the count of clusters in variance calculations) reduces bias in variance estimation when the number of clusters is small (e.g., k < 10 per arm)
Treatment and control rates are both specified per unit exposure (child-week), enabling direct comparison on a uniform rate scale
Risk difference Δ = 0.005 − 0.010 = −0.005 per child-week; absolute effect magnitude is 50% relative reduction
Output will be the smallest integer k (clusters per arm) that achieves at least 90% power under the specified conditions

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation
# with additive one-cluster correction for sample size calculation
# 
# Reference: Hayes & Moulton (2009) and related cluster-randomized trial methods
# Input parameters
p_t <- 0.005        # Treatment rate (events per child-week)
p_c <- 0.010        # Control rate (events per child-week)
E <- 2500           # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.15       # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05       # Two-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.90 # Target power
ratio <- 1          # Allocation ratio (1:1)

# For two-sided test with equal allocation
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)      # One-sided critical value for power

# Risk difference
delta <- p_t - p_c  # = -0.005 per child-week

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu_t <- p_t * E     # Treatment: 0.005 * 2500 = 12.5 events
mu_c <- p_c * E     # Control: 0.010 * 2500 = 25 events

# Variance under Poisson within-cluster + between-cluster CV
# For a rate parameter lambda with CV κ, the variance is (1 + κ^2) * lambda
# This accounts for: Poisson variance = lambda + extra-Poisson variance = lambda * κ^2

# Variance per cluster for treatment (per child-week scale)
var_t_per_unit <- p_t * (1 + kappa^2)  # Variance of rate per child-week

# Variance per cluster for control
var_c_per_unit <- p_c * (1 + kappa^2)

# Variance of cluster-level total counts
var_t_count <- (var_t_per_unit) * E    # Variance of total events in treatment cluster
var_c_count <- (var_c_per_unit) * E    # Variance of total events in control cluster

# Variance of cluster-level rates (counting expected events E per cluster)
# var(delta_hat) = var_t/n_t + var_c/n_c for risk difference
# where var_t = var(total events in treatment cluster) / E^2

# For cluster-aggregated rate difference estimator:
# var(p_t_hat) = (p_t * (1 + kappa^2)) / n_t  per cluster
# var(p_c_hat) = (p_c * (1 + kappa^2)) / n_c  per cluster

# Standard error squared of risk difference with k clusters per arm:
# SE^2(delta_hat) = [p_t * (1 + κ^2) + p_c * (1 + κ^2)] / k (for equal allocation)

# Additive one-cluster correction: k_eff = k + 1
# This corrects the variance estimate by replacing k with (k + 1) in the denominator

# Sample size formula (before rounding, without correction):
# n = 2 * (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * (p_t * (1 + κ^2) + p_c * (1 + κ^2)) / (delta)^2
# Note: 2 factor accounts for having 2 arms (k per arm)

# Combined variance (per arm, using rate scale)
combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)

# Uncorrected sample size formula (continuous)
k_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)

cat("=== Cluster-Rate CV Approximation with One-Cluster Correction ===\n\n")
cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate (p_t): %.4f events/child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate (p_c):   %.4f events/child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference:      %.4f events/child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster: %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV:   %.4f\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Two-sided alpha:      %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power:         %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:     %d:1\n", ratio))
cat("\nStatistical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2) [two-sided]:  %.4f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_β [power]:          %.4f\n", z_beta))
cat("\nVariance Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  p_t * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_t * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  p_c * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  Combined variance:    %.6f\n", combined_var))
cat("\nSample Size Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  (z_α/2 + z_β)²:       %.4f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator (z sum)² * var: %.6f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var))
cat(sprintf("  (delta)²:             %.8f\n", delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (uncorrected): %.4f\n", k_continuous))

# With additive one-cluster correction: solve for k such that (k + 1) satisfies power
# We need: (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / (k_corrected) = delta^2
# where k_corrected = k + 1
# So: k + 1 = (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / delta^2
# Thus: k = [(z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / delta^2] - 1

k_corrected_continuous <- k_continuous - 1

cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (one-cluster corrected): %.4f\n", k_corrected_continuous))

# Find minimum integer k that meets power requirement
# Check power at integer values
power_check <- function(k) {
  k_eff <- k + 1  # Additive one-cluster correction
  se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
  z_stat <- abs(delta) / se_delta
  power <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(z_alpha_2 - z_stat))  # Two-sided power
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum k
k_min <- 1
k_test <- seq(1, 30)
powers <- sapply(k_test, power_check)

# Find smallest k with power >= target
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
k_optimal <- k_test[idx]
power_at_optimal <- powers[idx]

# Also check preceding value for context
k_preceding <- k_optimal - 1
power_at_preceding <- if (k_preceding >= 1) power_check(k_preceding) else NA

cat("\n=== Integer Sample Size Search ===\n")
cat("Clusters/Arm | Achieved Power\n")
for (i in which(k_test %in% c(k_preceding, k_optimal, k_optimal+1))) {
  if (!is.na(k_test[i])) {
    cat(sprintf("     %2d      |    %.4f\n", k_test[i], powers[i]))
  }
}

cat(sprintf("\n*** RESULT: %d clusters per arm ***\n", k_optimal))
cat(sprintf("    Achieved power: %.4f\n", power_at_optimal))
if (k_preceding >= 1) {
  cat(sprintf("    Power at k=%d (preceding): %.4f\n", k_preceding, power_at_preceding))
}

# Output for structured reporting
results_df <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = k_optimal,
  unit = "clusters_per_arm"
)

cat("\n=== Structured Output ===\n")
print(results_df)

# This documents the statistical approach and validates the result

cat("=== METHODOLOGICAL DETAILS ===\n\n")

cat("Primary Estimand: Risk Difference in Cluster-Level Rates (per child-week)\n")

cat("  H0: λ_treatment = λ_control (rates equal across arms)\n")
cat("  H1: λ_treatment ≠ λ_control (two-sided alternative)\n")
cat("  Significance level: α = 0.05 (two-sided)\n\n")

cat("Analytical Method: Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation Approximation\n")
cat("  Reference: Hayes & Moulton (2009) and variations thereof\n")
cat("  Accounts for: Between-cluster heterogeneity in rate parameters\n")
cat("  Correction: Additive one-cluster correction to variance estimate\n\n")

# Parameters
p_t <- 0.005
p_c <- 0.010
E <- 2500
kappa <- 0.15
delta <- p_t - p_c

cat("Effect Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate λ_t:        %g per child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate λ_c:          %g per child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference (δ):       %g per child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Relative difference:       %.1f%% (treatment vs control)\n", 100 * delta / p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Expected events/cluster (treatment):  %.1f\n", p_t * E))
cat(sprintf("  Expected events/cluster (control):    %.1f\n", p_c * E))
cat("\nNuisance/Design Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster (E):  %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV (κ):    %.3f (multiplicative random effect)\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:          1:1 (equal allocation)\n\n")

z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - 0.05 / 2)
z_beta <- qnorm(0.90)

cat("Critical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2) = z_%.4f:         %.6f [two-sided rejection boundary]\n", 0.975, z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_β = z_%.4f:              %.6f [power-based quantile]\n", 0.90, z_beta))
cat(sprintf("  (z_(α/2) + z_β)²:          %.6f\n\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))

cat("Variance Calculation (Rate Scale):\n")
cat("  Under mixed model (Poisson within + log-normal between clusters):\n")

# Independent verification of the cluster-rate CV approximation result
# Using the formula and corrected two-sided power calculation

# Study parameters (from request)
p_t <- 0.005         # treatment rate (events per child-week)
p_c <- 0.010         # control rate (events per child-week)
E <- 2500            # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.15        # between-cluster CV
alpha <- 0.05        # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90 # target power
delta <- p_t - p_c   # risk difference = -0.005

# Critical values
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # 1.9600
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)     # 1.2816

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  p_t = %g, p_c = %g, delta = %g\n", p_t, p_c, delta))
cat(sprintf("  E = %d, kappa = %.3f\n", E, kappa))
cat(sprintf("  alpha = %.4f (two-sided), target power = %.2f\n", alpha, target_power))
cat(sprintf("  z_(alpha/2) = %.6f, z_beta = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, z_beta))

# Variance structure
# For rate lambda with between-cluster CV kappa:
# var(lambda) = lambda * (1 + kappa^2)

combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)
cat(sprintf("\nVariance of rate difference:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Combined var = (%.4f + %.4f) * (1 + %.4f^2) = %.6f\n", 
            p_t, p_c, kappa, combined_var))

# Sample size formula (uncorrected)
# k = [(z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * var] / (delta^2)
k_uncorrected <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)

cat(sprintf("\nUncorrected sample size:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  k = [(%.6f + %.6f)^2 * %.6f] / (%.8f)^2\n",
            z_alpha_2, z_beta, combined_var, delta))
cat(sprintf("  k = [%.6f * %.6f] / %.8f\n",
            (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2, combined_var, delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  k = %.4f clusters/arm (uncorrected)\n", k_uncorrected))

# Apply one-cluster correction (subtract 1)
k_corrected_continuous <- k_uncorrected - 1
cat(sprintf("\nWith additive one-cluster correction:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  k_corrected = %.4f - 1 = %.4f\n", k_uncorrected, k_corrected_continuous))

# Now find minimum integer k meeting power requirement
# Power function for two-sided test:
# Under H1 (delta ≠ 0): test statistic ~ N(delta/SE, 1)
# Reject H0 if |test_stat| > z_alpha/2
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha/2) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2) where Z ~ N(delta/SE, 1)

power_calc <- function(k) {
  k_eff <- k + 1  # effective clusters with correction
  se_delta <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff)
  ncp <- abs(delta) / se_delta  # non-centrality
  
  # Two-sided power: probability of rejecting H0 under alternative
  # = P(Z > z_alpha/2 | Z ~ N(ncp, 1)) + P(Z < -z_alpha/2 | Z ~ N(ncp, 1))
  pow <- pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE) +
         pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)
  
  return(pow)
}

# Search around the corrected continuous value
k_start <- floor(k_corrected_continuous) - 2
k_end <- floor(k_corrected_continuous) + 5
k_search <- seq(k_start, k_end, by = 1)

powers <- sapply(k_search, power_calc)

cat(sprintf("\n=== POWER SEARCH ===\n"))
cat("k (clusters/arm) | Power (two-sided)\n")
cat(paste(rep("-", 35), collapse = ""), "\n")
for (i in seq_along(k_search)) {
  marker <- if (powers[i] >= target_power & (i == 1 || powers[i-1] < target_power)) " <-- MINIMUM" else ""
  cat(sprintf("    %5d        | %.6f%s\n", k_search[i], powers[i], marker))
}

# Find minimum k
idx_min <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
k_minimum <- k_search[idx_min]
power_at_minimum <- powers[idx_min]
power_preceding <- if (idx_min > 1) powers[idx_min - 1] else NA

cat(sprintf("\n=== RESULT ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Minimum integer k (clusters per arm): %d\n", k_minimum))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f (target: %.2f)\n", power_at_minimum, target_power))
if (!is.na(power_preceding)) {
  cat(sprintf("Power at k=%d (preceding): %.6f\n", k_minimum - 1, power_preceding))
}

# Detailed verification at k=6446
cat(sprintf("\n=== VERIFICATION AT k = %d ===\n", k_minimum))
k_eff_min <- k_minimum + 1
se_min <- sqrt(combined_var / k_eff_min)
ncp_min <- abs(delta) / se_min

cat(sprintf("Effective clusters (k+1): %d\n", k_eff_min))
cat(sprintf("SE(delta): %.8f\n", se_min))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality: %.6f\n", ncp_min))
cat(sprintf("z_alpha/2: %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("P(Z > z_alpha/2 | ncp): %.6f\n", 
            pnorm(z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_min, sd = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)))
cat(sprintf("P(Z < -z_alpha/2 | ncp): %.6f\n",
            pnorm(-z_alpha_2, mean = ncp_min, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Total power (two-sided): %.6f\n", power_at_minimum))

# Compare with candidate answer
cat(sprintf("\n=== COMPARISON WITH CANDIDATE ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Candidate reported: k = 6446, power = 0.900031\n"))
cat(sprintf("Independent verification: k = %d, power = %.6f\n", k_minimum, power_at_minimum))
cat(sprintf("Match: %s\n", if (k_minimum == 6446 && abs(power_at_minimum - 0.900031) < 0.00001) "YES" else "NO"))

# Emit structured output
output_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_minimum, unit = "clusters_per_arm")
  )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)
cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=%s\n", output_json))

# Input parameters

p_c <- 0.010        # Control rate (events per child-week)
E <- 2500           # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)

# Risk difference

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu_t <- p_t * E     # Treatment: 0.005 * 2500 = 12.5 events
mu_c <- p_c * E     # Control: 0.010 * 2500 = 25 events

# Variance under Poisson within-cluster + between-cluster CV
# For a rate parameter lambda with CV κ, the variance is (1 + κ^2) * lambda
# This accounts for: Poisson variance = lambda + extra-Poisson variance = lambda * κ^2

# Variance per cluster for treatment (per child-week scale)
var_t_per_unit <- p_t * (1 + kappa^2)  # Variance of rate per child-week

# Variance per cluster for control
var_c_per_unit <- p_c * (1 + kappa^2)

# Variance of cluster-level total counts
var_t_count <- (var_t_per_unit) * E    # Variance of total events in treatment cluster
var_c_count <- (var_c_per_unit) * E    # Variance of total events in control cluster

# Variance of cluster-level rates (counting expected events E per cluster)
# var(delta_hat) = var_t/n_t + var_c/n_c for risk difference
# where var_t = var(total events in treatment cluster) / E^2

# For cluster-aggregated rate difference estimator:
# var(p_t_hat) = (p_t * (1 + kappa^2)) / n_t  per cluster
# var(p_c_hat) = (p_c * (1 + kappa^2)) / n_c  per cluster

# Standard error squared of risk difference with k clusters per arm:
# SE^2(delta_hat) = [p_t * (1 + κ^2) + p_c * (1 + κ^2)] / k (for equal allocation)

# Additive one-cluster correction: k_eff = k + 1
# This corrects the variance estimate by replacing k with (k + 1) in the denominator

# Sample size formula (before rounding, without correction):
# n = 2 * (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * (p_t * (1 + κ^2) + p_c * (1 + κ^2)) / (delta)^2
# Note: 2 factor accounts for having 2 arms (k per arm)

# Combined variance (per arm, using rate scale)
combined_var <- (p_t + p_c) * (1 + kappa^2)

# Uncorrected sample size formula (continuous)
k_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var) / (delta^2)

cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Treatment rate (p_t): %.4f events/child-week\n", p_t))
cat(sprintf("  Control rate (p_c):   %.4f events/child-week\n", p_c))
cat(sprintf("  Risk difference:      %.4f events/child-week\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("  Exposure per cluster: %d child-weeks\n", E))
cat(sprintf("  Between-cluster CV:   %.4f\n", kappa))
cat(sprintf("  Two-sided alpha:      %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power:         %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio:     %d:1\n", ratio))
cat("\nStatistical Quantiles:\n")
cat(sprintf("  z_(α/2) [two-sided]:  %.4f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_β [power]:          %.4f\n", z_beta))
cat("\nVariance Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  p_t * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_t * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  p_c * (1 + κ²):       %.6f\n", p_c * (1 + kappa^2)))
cat(sprintf("  Combined variance:    %.6f\n", combined_var))
cat("\nSample Size Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  (z_α/2 + z_β)²:       %.4f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator (z sum)² * var: %.6f\n", (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var))
cat(sprintf("  (delta)²:             %.8f\n", delta^2))
cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (uncorrected): %.4f\n", k_continuous))

# With additive one-cluster correction: solve for k such that (k + 1) satisfies power
# We need: (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / (k_corrected) = delta^2
# where k_corrected = k + 1
# So: k + 1 = (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / delta^2
# Thus: k = [(z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 * combined_var / delta^2] - 1

cat(sprintf("  Clusters/arm (one-cluster corrected): %.4f\n", k_corrected_continuous))

  k_eff <- k + 1  # Additive one-cluster correction

plan.estimand: Number of clusters per arm for two-arm parallel cluster-randomized trial comparing event rates
plan.hypothesis: Two-sided test of equality between treatment rate (0.005 per child-week) and control rate (0.010 per child-week)
assumptions: Poisson process for event generation with rate heterogeneity across clusters
Between-cluster rate variation characterized by coefficient of variation CV = 0.15
Cluster-level rates follow log-normal or related distribution such that marginal variance equals (μ + σ²) where μ is mean rate and σ² is between-cluster variance
Equal exposure of 2500 child-weeks per cluster
Equal allocation (1:1) to treatment and control arms
Large-sample normal approximation valid for cluster-level rate estimates
Additive one-cluster correction applied to sample-size formula
scientific_notes: The cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation models between-cluster heterogeneity in event rates. With CV = 0.15, the between-cluster variance σ² = (CV × μ)² where μ is the cluster mean rate.
The effective variance per cluster combines within-cluster Poisson variance and between-cluster variance. Under the log-normal random-effects model, the marginal variance is approximately μ + σ².

The additive one-cluster correction (also called '1 + ε' term or intercept correction) adjusts the sample-size formula by adding approximately one cluster per arm to account for loss of degrees of freedom in estimation and finite-sample effects.
Total exposure per cluster (2500 child-weeks) is fixed; power depends on the rate difference, the cluster-level heterogeneity (CV), and the number of clusters needed to detect the difference.

# Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation (CV) Approximation
# with Additive One-Cluster Correction
# Reference: Hayes & Moulton (2009) and related methodology for clustered counts

# Input parameters
lambda_treatment <- 0.005      # Treatment rate (events per child-week)
lambda_control <- 0.010        # Control rate (events per child-week)
n_exposure <- 2500             # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
cv_between <- 0.15             # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05                  # Significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90           # Target power
z_alpha_2sided <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # z-critical for two-sided test
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)  # z-critical for power

# Expected cluster-level rates (Poisson mean per cluster)
mu_treatment <- lambda_treatment * n_exposure
mu_control <- lambda_control * n_exposure

# Between-cluster variance for each arm
# Under log-normal random effects: variance = (cv * mu)^2
sigma2_treatment <- (cv_between * mu_treatment)^2
sigma2_control <- (cv_between * mu_control)^2

# Effective variance per cluster (within-cluster Poisson + between-cluster)
# For a Poisson-lognormal model: marginal variance ≈ μ + σ²
var_treatment <- mu_treatment + sigma2_treatment
var_control <- mu_control + sigma2_control

# Effect size and variance of the difference
rate_diff <- lambda_treatment - lambda_control
cluster_diff <- mu_treatment - mu_control
var_diff <- var_treatment + var_control

# Standard error of the difference (per cluster-pair)
se_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

# Sample size formula from cluster-rate CV approximation
# (z_alpha + z_beta)² * (var_treatment + var_control) / (mu_treatment - mu_control)²
# This gives the effective sample size as if each cluster contributes fully

n_clusters_formula <- ((z_alpha_2sided + z_beta)^2 * var_diff) / (cluster_diff^2)

# Apply additive one-cluster correction (1 + ε adjustment)
# This is the Hayes-Moulton-style correction to account for finite-sample effects
# and loss of degrees of freedom
n_clusters_corrected <- n_clusters_formula + 1

# Round up to integer for actual number of clusters per arm
n_clusters_per_arm <- ceiling(n_clusters_corrected)

cat("=== Cluster-Rate CV Approximation Calculation ===\n")
cat("Treatment rate (λ_t):", lambda_treatment, "per child-week\n")
cat("Control rate (λ_c):", lambda_control, "per child-week\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster (n_e):", n_exposure, "child-weeks\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV:", cv_between, "\n\n")

cat("Expected cluster-level event counts:\n")
cat("  μ_treatment:", mu_treatment, "\n")
cat("  μ_control:", mu_control, "\n\n")

cat("Between-cluster variance:\n")
cat("  σ²_treatment:", sigma2_treatment, "\n")
cat("  σ²_control:", sigma2_control, "\n\n")

cat("Effective marginal variance (μ + σ²):\n")
cat("  Var_treatment:", var_treatment, "\n")
cat("  Var_control:", var_control, "\n\n")

cat("Rate difference:", rate_diff, "per child-week\n")
cat("Cluster-level difference:", cluster_diff, "\n")
cat("Variance of difference:", var_diff, "\n\n")

cat("Critical values:\n")
cat("  z_{α/2} (two-sided α=0.05):", z_alpha_2sided, "\n")
cat("  z_β (power=0.90):", z_beta, "\n\n")

cat("Sample-size calculation:\n")
cat("  Formula: (z_α + z_β)² × Var(diff) / (μ_diff)²\n")
cat("  n (before correction):", n_clusters_formula, "\n")
cat("  n (after 1-cluster correction):", n_clusters_corrected, "\n")
cat("  n per arm (integer):", n_clusters_per_arm, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at the selected design
z_achieved <- (cluster_diff / se_diff) * sqrt(n_clusters_per_arm / 2)
# For two-sided test at α=0.05, the non-centrality parameter determines power
power_achieved <- 1 - pnorm(z_alpha_2sided - z_achieved) + pnorm(-z_alpha_2sided - z_achieved)
# More precise: two-sided power
power_achieved_2sided <- pnorm(z_achieved - z_alpha_2sided) + pnorm(-z_achieved - z_alpha_2sided)

cat("=== Verification of Achieved Power ===\n")
cat("At n =", n_clusters_per_arm, "clusters per arm:\n")
cat("  Non-centrality (z-statistic):", z_achieved, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power (two-sided):", power_achieved_2sided, "\n\n")

# Also check power at n-1
n_prev <- n_clusters_per_arm - 1
if (n_prev > 0) {
  z_prev <- (cluster_diff / se_diff) * sqrt(n_prev / 2)
  power_prev <- pnorm(z_prev - z_alpha_2sided) + pnorm(-z_prev - z_alpha_2sided)
  cat("At n =", n_prev, "clusters per arm (preceding design):\n")
  cat("  Achieved power (two-sided):", power_prev, "\n\n")
}

# Final result
cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm:", n_clusters_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Total clusters:", 2 * n_clusters_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved_2sided, 4), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
result <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_clusters_per_arm,
  unit = "clusters_per_arm"
)

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(result),
  method = "cluster_rate_cv"
)

cat("\nJSON Output:\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation (CV) Approximation
# with Additive One-Cluster Correction
# Inverting to find sample size for target power

# Input parameters
lambda_treatment <- 0.005      # Treatment rate (events per child-week)
lambda_control <- 0.010        # Control rate (events per child-week)
n_exposure <- 2500             # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
cv_between <- 0.15             # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05                  # Significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90           # Target power
z_alpha_2sided <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # z-critical for two-sided test
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)  # z-critical for power

# Expected cluster-level rates (Poisson mean per cluster)
mu_treatment <- lambda_treatment * n_exposure
mu_control <- lambda_control * n_exposure

# Between-cluster variance for each arm
sigma2_treatment <- (cv_between * mu_treatment)^2
sigma2_control <- (cv_between * mu_control)^2

# Effective marginal variance (within-cluster Poisson + between-cluster)
var_treatment <- mu_treatment + sigma2_treatment
var_control <- mu_control + sigma2_control

# Effect size and variance of the difference
cluster_diff <- mu_treatment - mu_control
var_diff <- var_treatment + var_control

cat("=== Cluster-Rate CV Approximation: Sample Size Inversion ===\n")
cat("Treatment rate (λ_t):", lambda_treatment, "per child-week\n")
cat("Control rate (λ_c):", lambda_control, "per child-week\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster (n_e):", n_exposure, "child-weeks\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV:", cv_between, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Two-sided α:", alpha, "\n\n")

cat("Expected cluster-level event counts:\n")
cat("  μ_treatment:", mu_treatment, "\n")
cat("  μ_control:", mu_control, "\n\n")

cat("Effective marginal variance (μ + σ²):\n")
cat("  Var_treatment:", var_treatment, "\n")
cat("  Var_control:", var_control, "\n")
cat("  Total Var(diff):", var_diff, "\n\n")

cat("Critical values:\n")
cat("  z_{α/2} (two-sided α=0.05):", z_alpha_2sided, "\n")
cat("  z_β (power=0.90):", z_beta, "\n")
cat("  z_{α/2} + z_β:", z_alpha_2sided + z_beta, "\n\n")

# Standard sample-size formula (without correction):
# n = [(z_α + z_β)² × Var(diff)] / (cluster_diff)²
n_uncorrected <- ((z_alpha_2sided + z_beta)^2 * var_diff) / (cluster_diff^2)

cat("Sample-size formula (before rounding/correction):\n")
cat("  n = (z_α + z_β)² × Var(diff) / (μ_diff)²\n")
cat("  n (continuous):", n_uncorrected, "\n\n")

# The additive one-cluster correction is typically applied *after* the formula
# so that the final per-arm sample size = floor(n_formula) + 1
# However, for proper inversion, we need to find the integer n such that:
# power(n) ≥ 0.90
# The "one-cluster correction" is sometimes interpreted as:
#   1. Apply the standard formula, then add 1, OR
#   2. Apply an adjusted formula that includes the correction implicitly

# Following Hayes & Moulton and common practice:
# The correction is additive: n_final = n_formula + 1
# We then round up to the nearest integer.

n_with_correction <- n_uncorrected + 1
n_per_arm <- ceiling(n_with_correction)

cat("With additive one-cluster correction:\n")
cat("  n (continuous, after +1):", n_with_correction, "\n")
cat("  n per arm (integer, rounded up):", n_per_arm, "\n\n")

# Verification: compute achieved power at this sample size
# For two-sided test of rate difference using normal approximation:
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = |μ_diff| / SE × sqrt(n/2)
# where SE = sqrt(var_diff)

se_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

# Achieved power function
achieve_power <- function(n_arms) {
  z_stat <- abs(cluster_diff) / se_diff * sqrt(n_arms / 2)
  # Two-sided power: P(|Z| > z_α) where Z ~ N(λ, 1)
  power_2sided <- pnorm(z_stat - z_alpha_2sided) + pnorm(-z_stat - z_alpha_2sided)
  return(power_2sided)
}

power_achieved <- achieve_power(n_per_arm)
power_prev <- achieve_power(n_per_arm - 1)

cat("=== Verification of Achieved Power ===\n")
cat("At n =", n_per_arm, "clusters per arm:\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")
cat("  Meets 90% target:", power_achieved >= 0.90, "\n\n")

cat("At n =", n_per_arm - 1, "clusters per arm (preceding design):\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", round(power_prev, 4), "\n")
cat("  Meets 90% target:", power_prev >= 0.90, "\n\n")

# Check if we need to increase sample size
if (power_achieved < 0.90) {
  cat("WARNING: Current design does not achieve 90% power.\n")
  cat("Searching for minimum sample size...\n\n")
  
  # Binary search or linear search to find minimum n
  n_search <- n_per_arm + 1
  while (achieve_power(n_search) < 0.90 && n_search <= 50) {
    n_search <- n_search + 1
  }
  n_per_arm <- n_search
  power_achieved <- achieve_power(n_per_arm)
  power_prev <- achieve_power(n_per_arm - 1)
  
  cat("Adjusted sample size:", n_per_arm, "clusters per arm\n")
  cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm, ":", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")
  cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm - 1, ":", round(power_prev, 4), "\n\n")
}

cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm:", n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Total clusters:", 2 * n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n-1:", round(power_prev, 4), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
result <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_per_arm,
  unit = "clusters_per_arm"
)

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(result),
  method = "cluster_rate_cv"
)

cat("\nJSON Output:\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# The "additive one-cluster correction" in cluster randomized trial sample-size formulas
# can be interpreted in different ways. Let's explore the context:
#
# Hayes & Moulton (2009) and related literature use forms like:
# n = [formula] + c
# where c is a small correction (typically 1 for simple cluster designs).
#
# However, the standard form without explicit correction is:
# n = (z_α + z_β)² × (CV² + 1) × λ̄ / (λ₁ - λ₀)²
#
# where λ̄ is the average rate, λ₁ and λ₀ are the treatment and control rates,
# and CV is the between-cluster coefficient of variation.
#
# Let me recalculate using a clearer interpretation:
# The "effective variance" in the presence of clustering is:
# Var(rate) = λ + (CV × λ)²
# which accounts for both Poisson and between-cluster variation.
#
# The correction term (+1) may be applied to the effective number of clusters
# after accounting for the design effect.

# Input parameters
lambda_t <- 0.005      # Treatment rate (events per child-week)
lambda_c <- 0.010      # Control rate (events per child-week)
n_exposure <- 2500     # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
cv_between <- 0.15     # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05          # Significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90   # Target power
z_alpha_2sided <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)

# Expected cluster-level rates
mu_t <- lambda_t * n_exposure
mu_c <- lambda_c * n_exposure

# Between-cluster variance components
sigma2_t <- (cv_between * mu_t)^2
sigma2_c <- (cv_between * mu_c)^2

# Effective variance (accounting for Poisson + random effects)
var_t <- mu_t + sigma2_t
var_c <- mu_c + sigma2_c
var_diff <- var_t + var_c

# Cluster-level rate difference
mu_diff <- mu_t - mu_c

cat("=== Interpretation of One-Cluster Correction ===\n\n")
cat("The one-cluster correction in cluster-randomized designs typically addresses:\n")
cat("1. Finite-sample effects in the test statistic distribution\n")
cat("2. Loss of degrees of freedom in cluster-level analysis\n")
cat("3. Conservative adjustment to ensure target power is met\n\n")

cat("Formula interpretation:\n")
cat("Standard form: n = (z_α + z_β)² × Var(diff) / (μ_diff)²\n\n")

# Calculate continuous sample size
n_continuous <- ((z_alpha_2sided + z_beta)^2 * var_diff) / (mu_diff^2)

cat("Continuous solution (no correction): n =", n_continuous, "\n\n")

# The additive one-cluster correction can mean:
# Option A: n_final = n_continuous + 1, then round up
# Option B: n_final = ceil(n_continuous + 1)
# Option C: A more sophisticated adjustment based on effective number of clusters

cat("One-cluster correction interpretations:\n")
cat("  A. n = n_continuous + 1, then round up: n =", ceiling(n_continuous + 1), "\n")
cat("  B. n = ceil(n_continuous) + 1: n =", ceiling(n_continuous) + 1, "\n\n")

# Given the literature context, Option B is often used:
# Round the uncorrected formula, then add 1 to account for finite-sample effects.

n_uncorrected_round <- ceiling(n_continuous)
n_final_interp_B <- n_uncorrected_round + 1

cat("Recommended interpretation (Hayes & Moulton style):\n")
cat("  n_uncorrected = ceil(n_formula) =", n_uncorrected_round, "\n")
cat("  n_final = n_uncorrected + 1 =", n_final_interp_B, "\n\n")

# However, if this still doesn't meet the target power, we need to search

se_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

achieve_power <- function(n_arms) {
  z_stat <- abs(mu_diff) / se_diff * sqrt(n_arms / 2)
  power_2sided <- pnorm(z_stat - z_alpha_2sided) + pnorm(-z_stat - z_alpha_2sided)
  return(power_2sided)
}

# Check both interpretations
power_optA <- achieve_power(ceiling(n_continuous + 1))
power_optB <- achieve_power(n_final_interp_B)

cat("Achieved power verification:\n")
cat("  Option A: n =", ceiling(n_continuous + 1), ", power =", round(power_optA, 4), "\n")
cat("  Option B: n =", n_final_interp_B, ", power =", round(power_optB, 4), "\n\n")

# If neither meets target, find minimum n that achieves 90% power
if (max(power_optA, power_optB) < 0.90) {
  cat("Neither interpretation achieves target power.\n")
  cat("Finding minimum n for 90% power...\n\n")
  
  n_min <- max(ceiling(n_continuous + 1), n_final_interp_B) + 1
  while (achieve_power(n_min) < 0.90 && n_min <= 50) {
    n_min <- n_min + 1
  }
  
  n_selected <- n_min
  power_selected <- achieve_power(n_selected)
  power_prev <- achieve_power(n_selected - 1)
  
} else {
  # Use the more conservative interpretation
  n_selected <- n_final_interp_B
  power_selected <- achieve_power(n_selected)
  power_prev <- achieve_power(n_selected - 1)
}

cat("=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm:", n_selected, "\n")
cat("Total clusters:", 2 * n_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_selected, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n-1 =", n_selected - 1, ":", round(power_prev, 4), "\n")

# JSON output
result <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_selected,
  unit = "clusters_per_arm"
)

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(result)
)

cat("\nJSON Output:\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
